points.description: States TRUE (the process may not be scheduled immediately after the interrupt handler finishes).

Justification: another process may be scheduled after the handler because the interrupted process's time slice expired during interrupt handling (or a scheduling/preemption decision, e.g. a higher-priority process, caused a different process to run).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the answer says a different process may run after the interrupt but gives a vague or incomplete reason.

rubric.notes: Full marks: TRUE with a reason that the scheduler may pick a different process after the handler, e.g. the time slice ended during the interrupt. Part marks: TRUE with a vague reason such as "the scheduler may choose another process". No marks if the answer says FALSE or gives no justification.
